correctness.rationale: The polar support gives dual norm N*(a,b)=|a|+|b| for ab≥0 and sqrt(a²+b²) for ab≤0. For square edges x=(1,t), 0≤t<1, forced y=(0,±1) yields quotient distance 1/sqrt(1+t²)≥1/sqrt2. Smooth circle branch x=(c,-s), c≥s>0, forced unit y=(s/c,1) yields (1+r²)/(1+r)≥2(sqrt2-1)>1/sqrt2. Square corner x=(1,1) has full segment of norming functionals, yielding Birkhoff y=(c,-s), c²+s²=1 and distance (c+s)/sqrt2≥1/sqrt2, attained by y=(1,0). Axes are smooth endpoint limits with forced axis Birkhoff directions and distance 1, so no omitted smaller case. Analytical complete stratum proof.

evidence: For every real two-dimensional Banach X, let d(X)=inf_{x perpendicular_B y, ||x||=||y||=1}dist(y,Rx). Given such x,y choose f in S(X*) norming x and annihilating y, and g in S(X*) annihilating x. The one-dimensional quotient identity gives dist_X(y,Rx)=|g(y)|. Since f perpendicular_B* g (normed by x), the dual reverse distance dist_(X*)(g,Rf) also equals |g(y)| because its annihilator is y in X**. The dual construction is reversible in dimension 2, so d(X)=d(X*). The Day-James ell2-ell1 dual norm is sqrt(p²+q²) for pq>=0 and max(|p|,|q|) for pq<=0. Reflecting q to -q turns it into the displayed square-circle norm, hence the two published numerical theorems are equivalent, not independent new claims.
The 2020 Remark 3.15 supplies the previously known failure of global C-approximate symmetry for the same l2-linf geometry.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Day–James D result implies the D half; 2020 paper implies the C contrast. No uncovered assertion remains.
